title: Penguin inheritance basic
notes: Classic exception to general rule; specificity should defeat general rule.

title: Military penguins override
notes: A subclass with a positive exception that should override the penguin exception.

title: Conflicting subclass rules
premises: Mammals give birth to live young.
Bat-owl is bat-like and an owl.
notes: Multiple inheritance from bat and owl families, both flying.

title: Contradiction from two parents
premises: Typically, B entities do not P.
X is both an A and a B.
notes: Test equal-ranked conflicting defaults from two parents.

title: Priority by rank
notes: Demonstrates ranking preference (higher numeric rank weaker).

title: Inherited exception chain
premises: Typically, Schooner-birds are heavy and do not fly.
notes: Ambiguous between heavyweight exception and juvenile exception.

title: Diamond inheritance with opposing defaults
premises: Leaf inherits from Left and Right.
notes: Both intermediate nodes provide same negative default.

title: Diamond with conflicting intermediates
premises: Leaf inherits from Left and Right.
notes: Requires defeat ordering or specificity tiebreak.

title: Specificity wins over strength
notes: Specific action should override general 'fly'.

title: Conflicting deep inheritance
premises: X is instance of A and D.
notes: Deep chains produce competing influences.

title: Trusted vs untrusted source
notes: Higher source reliability should tilt verdict.

title: Many weak sources vs one strong
notes: Single strong contradicting source should win unless aggregation policy differs.

title: Source reliability tie
notes: Equal reliability conflicting claims should lead to CONFLICT or UNKNOWN.

title: Aggregate weak support
premises: Ten weak reports each r=0.15 say Q.
notes: Test aggregation rule — whether many weaks can produce acceptance.

title: Temporal reliability shift
notes: Tests interaction of recency vs reliability.

title: Chain of trust
notes: Trust propagation and transitive reliability.

title: Source with partial reliability
notes: Close reliability values should produce ambiguous result.

title: Misinformation cascade
premises: Many low-quality mirrors repeat claim T (r=0.1 each).
One authoritative refutation (r=0.95) says not T.
notes: Authority should defeat cascaded low-reliability claims.

title: Old strong belief vs recent weak override
notes: Older high-confidence claim may persist despite recent weak override.

title: Recency beats old strong
notes: Two high-confidence contradictory claims at different times.

title: Decay leading to abstention
notes: Belief should decay to UNKNOWN if not reinforced.

title: Gradual override
notes: Multiple later supports for not D gradually override original D.

title: Activation threshold test
notes: Edge threshold between retention and overturning.

title: Temporal aggregation
notes: Later stronger evidence should overcome multiple earlier moderate supports.

title: Short-lived spike
notes: Rapid contradictory signals cause conflict.

title: Decay plus reinforcement
notes: Reinforcement after partial decay should recover acceptance.

title: Simple cycle
notes: Ensure cycles do not explode and that defaults are preserved.

title: Cycle with exception
notes: Conflicting defaults in cycle produce nuanced outcome.

title: Cycle with specificity
notes: Specific child exception should persist across cycle.

title: Mutually recursive defaults
notes: Mutual recursion with opposing defaults.

title: Large taxonomy cycle
premises: Chain of 6 classes A->B->C->D->E->F->A with mixed defaults.
notes: Stress test inference with long cycles.

title: Exception that closes the cycle
premises: C->A but C has exception not P.
notes: Complex closure of cycle with exceptions.

title: No evidence
notes: Baseline: no inputs should yield UNKNOWN.

title: Balanced weak evidence
premises: Two weak sources say S (r=0.2 each).
Two weak sources say not S (r=0.2 each).
notes: Balanced weak evidence should lead to CONFLICT/UNKNOWN.

title: Soft support without commitment
notes: Below acceptance threshold should abstain.

title: Conflicting strong supports
notes: High-confidence conflict should produce CONFLICT.

title: Abstention vs explicit no
notes: Explicit negative should produce NO even if other rules abstain.

title: Partial abstention aggregation
premises: Many abstentions and one weak positive.
notes: Aggregation of abstentions should not create false confidence.

title: Abstain vs low negative
premises: Abstain signals and a few low-confidence negatives.
notes: Low negatives plus abstention may tip to NO depending on policy.

title: Ambiguity propagation
premises: Upstream ambiguous evidence for property Q propagates downstream.
notes: Test ambiguity flow through inference chains.

title: Combinatorial rule expansion
premises: 10 independent weak defaults each implying R when combined pairwise produce proliferation of arguments.
notes: Stress test on argument generation and pruning.

title: Redundant derivations
premises: Multiple derivation paths yield same conclusion through slightly different assumptions.
notes: Ensures dedup/pruning of equivalent arguments.

title: Cross-coupled rules
premises: Rules mutually create each other's premises leading to many circular argument forms.
notes: Require cycle detection and pruning.

title: Large conjunctions
premises: Conclusions require large conjunctions of many weak facts.
notes: Combinatorial explosion test for conjunctive rules.

title: Filtered majority
premises: 100 small rules vote for V with slight contradictions.
notes: Test efficient aggregation under explosion.

title: Reliability + inheritance clash
premises: According to SourceA (reliability=0.95), Penguins do not fly.
According to SourceB (reliability=0.7), Military penguins fly.
notes: Combine source reliability with inheritance exceptions.

title: Activation, reliability, and abstention
notes: Test interplay of time, confidence, and reliability.

title: Deep inheritance + cycle
premises: Long inheritance chain with a back-edge creating a cycle and an exception halfway.
notes: Stress multi-factor interaction.

title: Adversarial default ordering
premises: Several defaults of varying ranks and specificities deliberately arranged to test tiebreak heuristics.
notes: Evaluate defeat ordering.

title: Multiple-source temporal war
premises: Interleaved time-stamped claims from multiple sources with different reliabilities.
notes: Complex real-world like scenario.
